title: Allow only the public read
summary: A SELECT policy can make fictional sample rows readable to the anon role.
introduction: A SELECT policy can make fictional sample rows readable to the anon role. Your task: Name the operations this policy does not allow.
learningObjectives: Name the operations this policy does not allow.
Explain the example for allow only the public read

blocks.text: A SELECT policy can make fictional sample rows readable to the anon role. Separate SQL privileges and RLS both matter.

Use the Supabase local CLI with its required container runtime, then run supabase init and supabase start in a practice project. Use the local URL and public key reported by its status command. SQL runs in the local database tools.

blocks.code:
GRANT SELECT ON public.cma_books TO anon;
CREATE POLICY "Read public sample books" ON public.cma_books FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true);
blocks.title: Allow only the public read

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A SELECT policy covers reads. It does not grant insert, update or delete operations.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The anon client can read these public sample books. This policy does not grant insert, update or delete access.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: USING(true) makes these rows public. Use it only for content deliberately intended for every visitor.

blocks.text: Name the operations this policy does not allow.
